purpose: Per-gene mass-spectrometry evidence for a translated protein product, genome-wide, from a REAL re-search of public raw spectra against a database that contains the 717 proteins. Replaces the Tier-1 string-match layer the atlas shipped from 2026-09-06.

corrections_2026_09_21.what: Three statements in this record were wrong and are corrected below. The per-gene data was never affected: it already reproduced the owning analysis's aspen_detection_by_class.tsv cell for cell.
corrections_2026_09_21.database: The searches this layer ships were run against 135,843 targets, not 98,659: the Tier 2 set plus a P. tremula Potra02 proteome (ms2-lsg analyses/proteomics_translation_evidence/RUN_LOG.md, 'All five datasets now searched under one database (135,843 targets)'). what_tier_2_is below still describes the original Tier 2 search.
corrections_2026_09_21.withdrawn_hit: Under the expanded database one of the two published Tier 2 pool hits, PtXaTreH.14G041300, no longer passes 1% FDR, and the owning analysis withdrew it on 2026-09-09. The headline below used to quote the published Tier 2 figure, 0.12% of the pool (2 of 1,611), pooled over haplotypes. The layer's own PXD025636 data gives 1 of 776 HAP1 and 0 of 835 HAP2.
corrections_2026_09_21.cross_species: The caveat below used to name PXD002544 and PXD058986 as containing no 717 protein. Those two are P. x canescens, 717's own cross. The datasets from other species are PXD025636 (P. trichocarpa), PXD020099 (P. tremula x tremuloides) and PXD025418 (P. tomentosa), as the owning analysis states.

why_public: Five public PRIDE datasets, re-searched with Sage (Apache-2.0). No wet-lab data of ours, no unpublished phenotype. The 717 proteome is already published on Phytozome.
join_key: gene_id + hap, matches the atlas gene index

why_this_replaces_the_tier_1_layer.what_tier_1_was: String-matching a 717 protein's tryptic peptides against peptide tables a third party produced by searching a DIFFERENT species' database (PXD023826, PXD025636, PXD064017).
why_this_replaces_the_tier_1_layer.the_structural_flaw: A Tier-1 negative is uninformative BY CONSTRUCTION. A peptide that exists only in 717 could never appear in a table built from another species' database, so 'not found' carries no information about whether the protein exists. The positives were really homology signals, not translation evidence.
why_this_replaces_the_tier_1_layer.what_tier_2_is: The raw spectra re-searched against a database that DOES contain the 717 proteins: 34,699 P. trichocarpa + 32,137 HAP1 + 31,823 HAP2 = 98,659 targets, source-prefixed, decoys generated by Sage. Now a negative is a real measurement.
why_this_replaces_the_tier_1_layer.what_is_lost_by_replacing: Tier 1 covered PXD023826 (hybrid aspen stem) and PXD064017 (xylem/tension-wood DIA), which are NOT among the five re-searched here. A ProteomeXchange census on 2026-09-09 established that neither is attemptable with this toolchain, which is a stronger reason than the earlier one and replaces it: PXD023826 is Waters SYNAPT G2-Si and PXD064017 is Bruker timsTOF HT, and no Linux reader for either vendor format exists here (both are vendor-DLL bound). PXD064017 is additionally DIA, which needs a DIA-specific engine rather than Sage. This matters beyond bookkeeping: all three Tier 1 hits came from PXD064017, so those three hits cannot currently be followed up by re-search at all. Stating the loss rather than leaving it implicit -- this layer is deeper and interpretable where Tier 1 was neither, but it is not a strict superset of datasets.

search.engine: Sage 0.14.7 (Lazear 2023, J Proteome Res), x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu build
search.engine_caveat: A Sage 1% FDR is not an MSFragger 1% FDR. The engines differ in scoring and decoy handling. The intended toolchain (MSFragger/FragPipe/Philosopher/Comet/MS-GF+/OpenMS) does not exist on this cluster and MSFragger additionally requires accepting an academic licence. Report the engine with the number.
search.fdr: 1% peptide-level AND 1% spectrum-level, both required, target PSMs only (label == 1)
search.parameters: read out of each dataset's own deposited search parameters, not guessed. For PXD025636 that meant catching TMT6plex +229.16293 on K and peptide N-term, which MaxQuant's parameters.txt does not list -- it is only visible in summary.txt as 'Reporter ion MS2' and in the channel count. Missing it would have failed almost silently, as a low identification rate rather than an error.

cross_species_caveat: PXD025636 is P. trichocarpa, PXD020099 is P. tremula x tremuloides and PXD025418 is P. tomentosa, so their samples contain no 717 protein at all. A peptide matching a 717 gene there is evidence that the GENE FAMILY is translated somewhere in Populus, not that 717's own copy is. For a Populus-genus-wide (PS18) gene that is the relevant question, but it is a different sentence and must be written as one. PXD002544 and PXD058986 are P. x canescens, the same P. tremula x P. alba cross as 717. (Corrected 2026-09-21; see corrections_2026_09_21.)
union_fdr_caveat: A fixed 1% per-dataset FDR ACCUMULATES across five datasets. Read a single-dataset singleton against the pooled false-peptide expectation (~1% of 121,308 peptide identifications), not against one dataset's.

the_detectability_column_is_the_control.why_it_exists: A protein with no fully-tryptic peptide in the searchable window, or none attributable to it uniquely, is invisible however abundant it is. That is a property of K/R content and length -- composition -- and lineage-specific genes differ from conserved genes in composition. Counting such a gene as 'not detected' inflates a negative exactly the way an unmatched control inflates an effect.
the_detectability_column_is_the_control.how_to_use_it: Read `detectable` before reading `n_datasets_detected == 0`. Undetectable genes should be excluded from a denominator, not corrected for.
the_detectability_column_is_the_control.measured_size_of_the_artifact: Small but real, and largest where it matters: 0.03-0.04% of ancient genes are undetectable against 0.92-1.46% of LSG-pool genes. So the raw and detectable-only rates differ by little (pool 0.0 vs 0.0, ancient 41.78 vs 41.79) and the powered negative survives the correction. Shipped anyway, because 'the control was run and it did not move the answer' is a different statement from 'no control was run'.

the_headline_this_layer_carries: Detection rate is monotone with gene age in both haplotypes. In the deepest dataset, PXD025636, it is 41.8% (HAP1) and 41.9% (HAP2) for PS1-2 ancient genes, 12.7% and 12.8% conserved, 5.3% and 6.6% rosid, 1.3% and 4.6% Salicaceae, and 1 of 776 HAP1 and 0 of 835 HAP2 LSG-pool genes -- the shape expected if the assay measures real protein abundance and conservation rather than noise. Across all five datasets the owning analysis reports PS18 2 of 433 HAP1 and 5 of 497 HAP2 against 15.46 and 30.86 expected at the PS16-17 rate (P = 3e-6 and 1e-9), and PS19 1 of 343 and 0 of 338 against 12.25 and 20.99 expected: a powered negative. Individual pool hits do not survive an adversarial read -- four of the eight genes carry glycine/serine low-complexity repeats, a known MS false-positive magnet, and the strongest is a gene already flagged as synteny-contested. One gene, PtXaTreH.01G189200, is a real lead: ordinary composition, two datasets, two species. (Corrected 2026-09-21; see corrections_2026_09_21.)
gate_run_on_every_build: make_proteomics_v2_source.py aggregates its own per-gene output back to gene class and compares it against the owning analysis's published aspen_detection_by_class.tsv, cell for cell. All 84 cells must match or nothing is written. The per-dataset PSM, peptide and gene counts independently reproduce that analysis's aspen_dataset_meta.json. This is what makes a locally derived table honest: not 'trust me', but 'it reproduces the number its owner published'.
detection_rule: Copied verbatim from ms2-lsg analyses/proteomics_translation_evidence/scripts/06_aspen_multidataset_readout.py: a target PSM (label == 1) at peptide_q <= 0.01 AND spectrum_q <= 0.01, mapped to every non-decoy protein it lists; gene = the first two dot-fields of the accession after its source prefix.
the_wider_resource_base: A live census on 2026-09-09 found 50 Salicaceae proteomics datasets (25 PRIDE, 14 iProX, 11 MassIVE); five are ingested here. Vendor format, not size, is the constraint: only 14 of the 25 PRIDE datasets are Thermo. About four more aspen-clade experiments are reachable for ~8 GB, two already as peak lists. See ms2-lsg docs/RESOURCE_CENSUS_20260909.md. Note also that PXD058986's depositors searched it against the 717 v5.1 haplotype proteome themselves -- the only one of the 25 to do so -- though it is a chitin affinity purification and so an enriched subproteome rather than a whole-proteome survey.
